validity.recommendation: Keep the row. Real, independently documented GASCO transmission spur; fix the capacity units and owner (below).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE = confirmed (high). 'Veunsa' is a transliteration of فينوسا (Finusa/Veunosa). The line is the 'Gamasa–Finusa gas line' (خط غاز جمصة - فينوسا), a 42-inch / 34 km GASCO transmission spur that taps room/valve station #10 on the existing Edco–Damietta 32" trunk at Gamasa and runs to the 32" valve inside the Finusa intake room (+ Imethanics), feeding the West Damietta (New West Damietta) power plant (8x125 MW = ~1,000 MW). Built by GASCO (contractor Petrojit), completed Nov 2015. Independently attested by youm7 (2016-02-26, the sheet's own ref), the Egyptian Presidency national-projects page (presidency.eg, official, names the line + 42"/34km/397M EGP + GASCO), and egy-map.com. Two+ independent origins agree on name, length, diameter, endpoints, executor. CLASSIFICATION = correct: gas transmission spur that is part of the national gas grid (الشبكة القومية للغازات) — a power-plant feeder but at trunk pressure/size, so 'transmission' is defensible. DUPLICATE = none: unique name, absent from the GulfPub Egypt roster; NOT the same as P6037 Al Gamil–Damietta (Port Said–area, different origin) nor any other Delta line in the roster.

validity.recommendation: Fix Capacity: 6.8 is million CUBIC METRES/day, not MMcf/d. Convert to ~240 MMcf/d, or record 6.8 Mm3/d. Current 6.80 MMcf/d is wrong by ~35x.
validity.researcher_notes: Both sources state the line supplies the West Damietta power plant with 6.8 مليون متر مكعب (6.8 MILLION CUBIC METRES) of gas per day. GEM copied the bare number '6.8' but labelled the units MMcf/d. 6.8 million m3/d = 6.8 x 35.3147 = ~240 MMcf/d. So GEM's Capacity=6.80 MMcf/d understates the documented flow by a factor of ~35. (A 42" line's physical capacity is far higher still; 240 MMcf/d is the stated power-plant supply figure.) Did not attach a ref to the current value because the value is unit-wrong.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner/Operator from 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) to GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company / الشركة المصرية للغازات). EGAS is the parent holding; GASCO built and operates this national-grid trunkline.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS, the parent holding company). Every source credits GASCO — the Egyptian Natural Gas Company — as the executor and grid operator of this line ("تم تنفيذه بواسطة جاسكو"). GASCO owns/operates Egypt's high-pressure transmission grid; EGAS is its parent. Per project convention (GASCO vs EGAS distinction), owner/operator of a transmission trunk should be GASCO. Not fatal (EGAS ultimately controls GASCO) but the specific attribution is wrong.

validity.recommendation: Review SegmentCost: GEM = 340,000,000 EGP but all sources state ~397 million EGP. Update to 397M EGP (2015) or confirm why 340M.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost = 340,000,000 EGP. youm7, presidency.eg and egy-map all give the cost as ~397 million EGP (completed Nov 2015). Consistent 397M across independent sources vs GEM's 340M — GEM's figure appears wrong (possibly an earlier contract/net figure). Did not attach a ref to 340M since sources disagree.

fills.researcher_notes: Completion/commissioning Nov 2015 (line built to feed the West Damietta plant, commissioned 2015). Both official (presidency.eg) and news (youm7) sources confirm 2015; StartYear1=2015 is correct.

Line runs within Egypt from Gamasa (start, room #10 on the Edco–Damietta 32" trunk) to the Finusa (فينوسا) intake feeding the West Damietta power plant. NOTE: Gamasa town itself sits at the Dakahlia/Damietta boundary (commonly Dakahlia Governorate); the destination West Damietta plant is in Damietta Governorate (Kafr Saad). GEM's StartState/Province='Damietta' is right for the endpoint/plant end; consider adding StartLocation='Gamasa' and EndLocation='West Damietta power plant (Finusa intake)'. Ref supports the Egypt/Damietta placement.

routes.start_name: Gamasa (station/room #10 on the Edco–Damietta 32" trunk), Dakahlia/Damietta coast
routes.end_name: Finusa (Veunsa) intake feeding the West Damietta power plant, Kafr Saad, Damietta
routes.corridor_desc: ~34 km trunk spur running NE along the Nile Delta Mediterranean-coast belt from the Gamasa tie-in (station #10 on the existing Edco–Damietta 32" line, ~31.145N 31.513E, on the Dakahlia coast) to the Finusa/Veunsa intake at the West Damietta (New West Damietta) power plant near Kafr Saad, Damietta Governorate (~31.442N 31.606E). Straight-line distance between these two named endpoints is ~33 km, matching the documented 34 km length, so the corridor is tightly bounded even without routed geometry. Intermediate routing (the actual pipe alignment across the coastal farmland/lagoon fringe of Dakahlia–Damietta) is not published; endpoints are firm, path is inferred.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named places in the sources: start = Gamasa tie-in on the Edco–Damietta 32" line; end = Finusa/Veunsa intake at the West Damietta power plant. Gamasa town coord (~31.145,31.513) is the well-known coastal-town centroid; West Damietta power-plant coord (~31.442,31.606) is the facility location reported by Global Energy Observatory. Both are real/defensible place centroids, NOT fabricated; the ~33 km separation matches the stated 34 km. No intermediate coordinates were invented — waypoints left empty because the pipe alignment is unpublished.

summary: P6035 Gamasa–Veunsa (=فينوسا/Finusa) is a REAL 42"/34km GASCO transmission spur (Gamasa→West Damietta power plant, 2015) — existence/classification/uniqueness confirmed high; concerns: Capacity 6.80 MMcf/d is a unit error (source=6.8 Mm3/d≈240 MMcf/d), Owner should be GASCO not EGAS, and cost is 397M EGP not 340M.
